name: hallmark
description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
readmeExcerpt:
# Hallmark **A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.** [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com)  ·  forty-eight themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name Made by Together AI.

Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of forty-eight materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word. The gates come in tiers. The **Floor** never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). **Reflex** gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. **Finish** checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship. ## New in v2 - **Forty-eight themes.** Each is a material (paper, type, colour, surfaces, its own components and texture) with a picture of a finished page, and the build lays out its own page in it. - **Built from the job.** A booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes: the action sits where the category puts it, and the page ends on it. - **Custom.** Ask for a custom page and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks. - **Your real product.** Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself. - **Real photographs.** 755 openly licensed photos, picked per subject and credited on the page. - **Redesign and audit.** `/hallmark redesign ` rebuilds a page and keeps its content and wiring; `/hallmark audit ` only reports. ## Themes
Dusk
Closewise, bank reconciliation		 Cobalt
Relay, a webhook API		 Studio
Field Office, an identity studio		 Atelier
Maison Orla, a fragrance atelier		 Ribbon
Lull, a sleep sounds app
Furrow
Fieldbook, farm records		 Dose
Tandem, a family medication app		 Hum
Sprout, a reading game for kids		 Terminal
burrow, a dotfiles CLI		 Hedgerow
Five Mile Gin, a distillery
Ten of the forty-eight. A theme is a material, not a plan: it never says what a page contains or in what order, so two prompts in one theme make two different pages. Each is one file of at most 8 KB in [`references/themes/`](skills/hallmark/references/themes/) with a picture beside it; a build reads exactly one. See them all at [usehallmark.com](https://www.usehallmark.com). ## Custom Say **custom** and Hallmark drops the themes: no plan, no components, no palette recipe, only the floor, the gates and a short direction in [`direction.md`](skills/hallmark/references/direction.md) to find one idea that only this client has and let it run the page. ## How a build runs 1. Pre-flight reads the project (fonts, palette, framework, a locked `design.md`) and asks once for the material: photos, screenshots, real numbers. Nothing is invented. 2. `scripts/theme.mjs deal` offers three themes that fit the prompt and clear the log; `draw` deals the page's anatomy from its job. 3. The hero is built alone, rendered and reviewed cold before the rest of the page exists. 4. `scripts/sloplint.mjs --render` checks the page at eight widths, then a subagent reviews it with fresh eyes. Each page is self-contained HTML and CSS, stamped in its first CSS comment with the decisions it took. ## Redesign Hallmark never starts on a design that already exists unless you name it: ``` /hallmark redesign ./src/app /hallmark audit ./index.html ``` A full redesign keeps the content and the wiring and changes the system and the layout; say *keep the layout* for a restyle or *polish* for only the tells. `sloplint --before` records every link, field, handler and heading first, `sloplint --kept` fails the redesign if one went missing, and the handoff is a side-by-side before and after. ## Install ``` npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g ``` `-g` installs for every project; leave it off to install into the current one. Needs Node 18 or later. The browser checks (`sloplint --render`, screenshots) also need `npm i -g puppeteer-core` and Chrome; without them the static checks still run. | Harness | Lands in | Invoke | | --- | --- | --- | | Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/hallmark` | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Codex CLI | `~/.agents/skills/hallmark` | `$hallmark ` or describe a new build | | Cursor | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | | OpenCode | finds the copies above | `/hallmark ` or describe a new build | - **One harness only:** `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-code` (or `codex`, `opencode`, `cursor`, `github-copilot`). - **As a Claude Code plugin:** `/plugin marketplace add nutlope/hallmark`, then `/plugin install hallmark@hallmark` (invoked as `/hallmark:hallmark`). - **From a clone:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/install.mjs` validates every theme and reference before it copies; `install-hook.mjs` adds an edit-time Floor check to Claude Code. - **Lint any page:** `node skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs --render`. - **If it does not fire on its own,** name it: *use hallmark to build ...*. ## Licence MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it. The photo library (`skills/hallmark/scripts/photos.json`) lists photographs hosted on Wikimedia Commons and holds no image files. Each keeps its own licence (CC0, public domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA), and Hallmark credits every one it uses on the page. It does not use stock sites (Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay), whose terms bar AI tools from picking their images.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A design skill for Claude Code that refuses to look AI-generated.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Hallmark is a specialized Agent Skill tailored for Claude Code, designed to ensure that generated UI components feel organic and human-crafted. It achieves this by explicitly instructing the AI to avoid common generative hallmarks—such as generic Tailwind styling, symmetrical grid layouts, and overused color palettes. Instead, it guides the model to adopt asymmetric designs, distinct typography, and nuanced spacing that mirror professional, bespoke frontend development. The tool essentially acts as a stylistic governor, forcing the AI to produce frontend code that breaks away from the predictable 'AI look'. It integrates directly into the Claude Code workflow via the standard Agent Skills format.
keyFeatures: Anti-Generative Styling: Employs targeted prompts that forbid the use of common, easily identifiable AI design tropes.
Asymmetric Layout Enforcement: Encourages the generation of varied, human-like layout structures over perfect, rigid grids.
Nuanced Typography Guidelines: Instructs the model to utilize specific typographic scales and distinct font pairings.
Claude Code Integration: Formatted precisely as an Agent Skill for seamless adoption within the Claude Code environment.
Bespoke Component Generation: Shifts the model's output toward creating highly customized, visually unique React components.

Hallmark

A design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that refuses to look AI-generated.

usehallmark.com  ·  forty-eight themes  ·  custom on request  ·  redesign and audit by name

Made by Together AI.

Hallmark holds a hard floor and then gets out of the way. It deals three themes from a catalog of forty-eight materials, builds the page around what the visitor came to do, and lints the result in a real browser against the tells that read as machine-made: the eyebrow above every heading, tracked-capital labels, one coloured word in a headline, a page of empty frames or nothing but photographs, a hero that misses its screen, an email sign-up at the end of every page, a form that says thanks without sending anything. A fresh-context reviewer gets the last word.

The gates come in tiers. The Floor never ships (contrast, focus, reduced motion, invented facts, a broken phone layout). Reflex gates are the defaults a model falls into; a build with a reason may overrule one on the record. Finish checks are craft detail that never blocks a ship.

New in v2

  • Forty-eight themes. Each is a material (paper, type, colour, surfaces, its own components and texture) with a picture of a finished page, and the build lays out its own page in it.
  • Built from the job. A booking page books, a shop sells, a newsletter subscribes: the action sits where the category puts it, and the page ends on it.
  • Custom. Ask for a custom page and Hallmark designs from your prompt alone, under the same rules and checks.
  • Your real product. Point it at a URL, a dev server or an app and it captures the screenshots itself.
  • Real photographs. 755 openly licensed photos, picked per subject and credited on the page.
  • Redesign and audit. /hallmark redesign <path> rebuilds a page and keeps its content and wiring; /hallmark audit <path> only reports.

Themes

Dusk
Closewise, bank reconciliation		 Cobalt
Relay, a webhook API		 Studio
Field Office, an identity studio		 Atelier
Maison Orla, a fragrance atelier		 Ribbon
Lull, a sleep sounds app
Furrow
Fieldbook, farm records		 Dose
Tandem, a family medication app		 Hum
Sprout, a reading game for kids		 Terminal
burrow, a dotfiles CLI		 Hedgerow
Five Mile Gin, a distillery

Ten of the forty-eight. A theme is a material, not a plan: it never says what a page contains or in what order, so two prompts in one theme make two different pages. Each is one file of at most 8 KB in references/themes/ with a picture beside it; a build reads exactly one. See them all at usehallmark.com.

Custom

Say custom and Hallmark drops the themes: no plan, no components, no palette recipe, only the floor, the gates and a short direction in direction.md to find one idea that only this client has and let it run the page.

How a build runs

  1. Pre-flight reads the project (fonts, palette, framework, a locked design.md) and asks once for the material: photos, screenshots, real numbers. Nothing is invented.
  2. scripts/theme.mjs deal offers three themes that fit the prompt and clear the log; draw deals the page's anatomy from its job.
  3. The hero is built alone, rendered and reviewed cold before the rest of the page exists.
  4. scripts/sloplint.mjs --render checks the page at eight widths, then a subagent reviews it with fresh eyes.

Each page is self-contained HTML and CSS, stamped in its first CSS comment with the decisions it took.

Redesign

Hallmark never starts on a design that already exists unless you name it:

/hallmark redesign ./src/app
/hallmark audit ./index.html

A full redesign keeps the content and the wiring and changes the system and the layout; say keep the layout for a restyle or polish for only the tells. sloplint --before records every link, field, handler and heading first, sloplint --kept fails the redesign if one went missing, and the handoff is a side-by-side before and after.

Install

npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g

-g installs for every project; leave it off to install into the current one. Needs Node 18 or later. The browser checks (sloplint --render, screenshots) also need npm i -g puppeteer-core and Chrome; without them the static checks still run.

Harness Lands in Invoke
Claude Code ~/.claude/skills/hallmark /hallmark <prompt> or describe a new build
Codex CLI ~/.agents/skills/hallmark $hallmark <prompt> or describe a new build
Cursor finds the copies above /hallmark <prompt> or describe a new build
OpenCode finds the copies above /hallmark <prompt> or describe a new build
  • One harness only: npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g --agent claude-code (or codex, opencode, cursor, github-copilot).
  • As a Claude Code plugin: /plugin marketplace add nutlope/hallmark, then /plugin install hallmark@hallmark (invoked as /hallmark:hallmark).
  • From a clone: node skills/hallmark/scripts/install.mjs validates every theme and reference before it copies; install-hook.mjs adds an edit-time Floor check to Claude Code.
  • Lint any page: node skills/hallmark/scripts/sloplint.mjs <file-or-dir> --render.
  • If it does not fire on its own, name it: use hallmark to build ....

Licence

MIT. Use it, fork it, ship it.

The photo library (skills/hallmark/scripts/photos.json) lists photographs hosted on Wikimedia Commons and holds no image files. Each keeps its own licence (CC0, public domain, CC BY or CC BY-SA), and Hallmark credits every one it uses on the page. It does not use stock sites (Unsplash, Pexels, Pixabay), whose terms bar AI tools from picking their images.
